scenario.title: Three facilities, one essential product
scenario.product: Synthetic essential medicine X (NOT a real product)
scenario.note: Synthetic warehouses, transport capacities, and demand. No medical recommendations.

legal_review.message: Candidate movements are NOT approved. Qualified local authorities must verify product registration, facility authority, required permits and distribution conditions. High-level policy announcements do not authorize a transfer.

policy_matrix.scope: research hypotheses only; not a determination that the law is missing

rows.title: Product and facility authorization for proposed redistribution
rows.trigger: Proposed movement of regulated medical product
rows.question: Who may approve an inter-facility movement of this exact product, and what are the prerequisites?
rows.proposed_research: Obtain binding UAE regulations and confirmation from qualified pharmaceutical counsel.

rows.title: Inter-institutional escalation and information-sharing protocol
rows.trigger: Earlier private update was subsequently disclosed
missing: formal disclosure timing and audit controls
rows.question: What are the permitted channels and escalation duties for supply alerts shared between institutions?
rows.proposed_research: Compare documented escalation mandates across agencies and suppliers.

rows.title: Data minimization, confidentiality and accountable AI sharing
rows.trigger: Cross-organization supplier disclosure and AI assessment
missing: full applicable privacy rules and exemptions
AI security policy applicability and governance approvals
rows.question: Which data may each actor disclose, to whom, and under what verified basis?
rows.proposed_research: Verify with current UAE binding data law, healthcare mandates and legal/privacy reviewers.

rows.title: Transferability of international shortage coordination practices
rows.question: Which coordination features in the EMA solidarity mechanism are reusable as design patterns?
rows.proposed_research: Map roles, data exchange, escalation and legal authority without transplanting EU law.

claim_references.claim: On 24 February 2026 EDE announced a mechanism requiring more than one authorized commercial agent for each marketed medical product, intended to reduce supply disruption risk. Commercial agents are not AI agents.

source.title: EDE multiple authorized commercial agents mechanism, 24 February 2026
source.summary: EDE announced activation of a mechanism requiring companies to appoint more than one authorized commercial agent for each medical product marketed in the UAE. These are commercial agents, not AI agents.

claim_references.claim: The EDE legislation index lists the federal law governing medical products, pharmacists and pharmaceutical establishments. The index alone does not determine the legality of a specific transfer.

source.title: EDE published legislation catalogue
source.summary: Official index includes federal legislation governing medical products and a national essential medicines list. The index alone does not establish permission for an inter-hospital transfer.

claim_references.claim: The EMA oversees an EU/EEA voluntary solidarity mechanism for assistance with medicine stocks during exceptional critical shortages. It is a comparative example, not a UAE transfer authorization.

source.title: EMA Voluntary Solidarity Mechanism for critical shortages
source.summary: A voluntary mechanism supports countries seeking assistance during exceptional critical shortages. Its procedures are not binding in the UAE.

claim_references.claim: The challenge expects sequenced information disclosure to differently informed institutional agents, plus auditability and an architecture mapping to Y.3172 and AI Readiness.

source.title: AI for Good Lab Hackathon UAE 2026 — evaluation criteria
source.summary: Official 2026 UAE hackathon evaluation requires national knowledge base, agent scenarios, global policy examples, evidence logs and Y.3172/AI readiness mapping.

claim_references.claim: The UAE AI Charter overview stresses responsible human-centered AI, privacy, transparency, safety and accountability. It is AI governance context, not an inter-hospital product transfer permission.

source.title: UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
source.summary: The official charter overview emphasizes responsible AI, privacy, safety, fairness, transparency, accountability and compliance with applicable law. Source is a policy overview, not product-specific approval.

claim_references.claim: The UAE National Cyber Security Policy for AI overview emphasizes operational safety, secure application lifecycle and human oversight for critical decisions. Its relevance to this prototype requires a detailed applicability review.

source.title: National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence
source.summary: The official overview covers AI operational safety, secure ML asset lifecycle, monitoring, resilience and human oversight in critical decisions. Full downloadable text is not bundled.

claim_references.claim: The UAE government cyber laws index lists Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 concerning personal data protection. Applicability and exemptions for any healthcare data processing require expert verification.

source.title: UAE cyber laws catalogue (including Federal Decree-Law No 45 of 2021 on personal data protection)
source.summary: Official cyber laws catalogue identifies the federal personal data protection law. The index does not establish applicability, exemptions or permitted processing for a specific inter-hospital exchange.

claim_references.claim: The WHO model essential medicines list was updated in September 2025; it guides national selection and does not itself authorize procurement, transfer, or substitution.

source.title: WHO Model List of Essential Medicines, 24th edition (2025)
source.summary: WHO maintains an essential medicines model list to guide country priorities. It is not a permit to distribute or substitute any specific product.
